newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Sioen sees expansion in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Sioen sees expansion in Asia.

text.p: Belgian textile firm Sioen Industries, whose shares traded on the Brussels bourse for the first time on Friday, said the new capital it raised would help it expand in southeast Asia.
"We came to the bourse to keep growing. We want to expand in the southeast Asian market," the company's founder and chairman Jean-Jacques Sioen said at a news conference.
The company was planning to buy a factory in Indonesia, Sioen told Reuters after the launch ceremony at the Brussels bourse.
Sioen shares were introduced on the bourse's second tier cash market where they were fixed at 1,580 francs, up 12.86 percent from the 1,400 franc issue price. Their price is fixed twice a day.
The initial public offering of 600,000 shares, or 30.1 percent, of Sioen's capital was five times oversubscribed.
Based in the northern Belgian Flanders region, the group says it is a European leader in the coating of textile products. It currently employs more than 1,000 workers in five countries.
